intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy-2 (CHN2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding myelin protein zero (MPZ; 159440) on chromosome 1q23.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy-2 (CHN2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the MPZ gene, which encodes myelin protein zero.
checks.evidence_quote: the identification of a mutation in the gene (MPZ) for protein zero (P0) associated with this phenotype are described
checks.explanation: The abstract links congenital hypomyelination to an MPZ mutation (Q215X) in one case. It does not state that the mutation is heterozygous or use the CHN2 designation.

checks.claim: The MPZ gene is located on chromosome 1q23.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations have been described in the following genes, MPZ, EGR2, PMP22, and MTMR2.
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the MPZ gene, which the paper names.

paragraphs.text: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a severe peripheral neuropathy that begins at birth or in early infancy. Affected infants have hypotonia, generalized weakness, areflexia, and very slow nerve conduction velocities. Nerve biopsy shows hypomyelination or absent myelin, without the active demyelination and remyelination that are typical of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1. CHN2 lies at the severe end of the range of MPZ-related neuropathies. The milder end of this range includes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B and Dejerine-Sottas neuropathy.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a severe peripheral neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy (CHN; MIM# 605253) is a severe neuropathy with early infancy onset
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy begins at birth or in early infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by prenatal, neonatal or early infantile onset of hypotonia, paresis and areflexia
checks.explanation: The abstract gives prenatal, neonatal or early infantile onset.

checks.claim: Infants with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy have hypotonia.
checks.evidence_quote: early infancy onset, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia
checks.explanation: The abstract lists hypotonia as a feature of CH.

checks.claim: Infants with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy have generalized weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia
checks.explanation: The abstract describes distal muscle weakness, not generalized weakness.

checks.claim: Infants with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy have areflexia.
checks.evidence_quote: distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia
checks.explanation: The abstract lists areflexia as a feature of CH.

checks.claim: Infants with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy have very slow nerve conduction velocities.
checks.evidence_quote: severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities
checks.explanation: 'Severe slowing' matches 'very slow' nerve conduction velocities.

checks.claim: Nerve biopsy in congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy shows hypomyelination or absent myelin.
checks.evidence_quote: Sural nerve biopsy shows a characteristic picture of nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons with basal lamina onion bulbs
checks.explanation: Nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons correspond to absent myelin and hypomyelination.

checks.claim: Nerve biopsy in congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy lacks the active demyelination and remyelination typical of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1.
checks.evidence_quote: with basal lamina onion bulbs and lack of myelin breakdown products
checks.explanation: The abstract notes a lack of myelin breakdown products but makes no comparison with CMT1 demyelination and remyelination.

checks.claim: CHN2 lies at the severe end of the range of MPZ-related neuropathies.
checks.evidence_quote: confirms that CH is allelic with other disorders characterized by a less severe phenotype
checks.explanation: If CH is allelic with less severe disorders, it lies at the severe end of the MPZ-related range.

checks.claim: The milder end of the range of MPZ-related neuropathies includes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B and Dejerine-Sottas neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: quite distinct from those of the more frequent Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 1B disease (CMT1B) or Dejerine-Sottas syndrome (DSS) confirms that CH is allelic with other disorders characterized by a less severe phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract names CMT1B and DSS as allelic disorders with a less severe phenotype.

paragraphs.text: CHN2 is transmitted in an autosomal dominant pattern. Reported cases have often arisen from de novo heterozygous MPZ mutations.

checks.claim: CHN2 is transmitted in an autosomal dominant pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: inherited as an autosomal dominant or recessive trait
checks.explanation: The abstract says CHN in general can be dominant or recessive; it does not say that CHN2 specifically is dominant.

checks.claim: Reported cases of CHN2 have often arisen from de novo heterozygous MPZ mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: This "de novo" mutation in a patient presenting with clinical features
checks.explanation: The abstract reports one de novo MPZ mutation in a single patient. It does not show that cases 'often' arise de novo, and it does not state that the mutation is heterozygous.

paragraphs.text: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is genetically heterogeneous. CHN1 is caused by mutation in the EGR2 gene, and CHN3 is caused by mutation in the CNTNAP1 gene.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Several mutations in the MTMR2, PMP22, EGR2, and MPZ genes have been found in patients with CHN.
checks.explanation: Mutations in multiple genes indicate genetic heterogeneity.

checks.claim: CHN1 is caused by mutation in the EGR2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Several mutations in the MTMR2, PMP22, EGR2, and MPZ genes have been found in patients with CHN.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists EGR2 mutations in CHN but does not use the CHN1 designation.

checks.claim: CHN3 is caused by mutation in the CNTNAP1 gene.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not mention CNTNAP1.

paragraphs.text: Warner et al. (1996) studied patients with inherited peripheral neuropathies and found heterozygous mutations in the MPZ gene in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B, Dejerine-Sottas syndrome, and congenital hypomyelination. They concluded that different MPZ mutations can produce a spectrum of clinical phenotypes, with congenital hypomyelination at the most severe end.

checks.claim: Warner et al. (1996) studied patients with inherited peripheral neuropathies.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified five novel mutations in the myelin protein zero (MPZ) gene, encoding the major structural protein (P0) of peripheral nerve myelin, in patients with either CMT1B, DSS, or CH.
checks.explanation: The patients studied had hereditary peripheral neuropathies.

checks.claim: Warner et al. (1996) found heterozygous MPZ mutations in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified five novel mutations in the myelin protein zero (MPZ) gene, encoding the major structural protein (P0) of peripheral nerve myelin, in patients with either CMT1B, DSS, or CH.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not state that the mutations were heterozygous.

checks.claim: Warner et al. (1996) found heterozygous MPZ mutations in patients with Dejerine-Sottas syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified five novel mutations in the myelin protein zero (MPZ) gene, encoding the major structural protein (P0) of peripheral nerve myelin, in patients with either CMT1B, DSS, or CH.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not state that the mutations were heterozygous.

checks.claim: Warner et al. (1996) found heterozygous MPZ mutations in patients with congenital hypomyelination.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified five novel mutations in the myelin protein zero (MPZ) gene, encoding the major structural protein (P0) of peripheral nerve myelin, in patients with either CMT1B, DSS, or CH.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not state that the mutations were heterozygous.

checks.claim: Warner et al. (1996) concluded that different MPZ mutations can produce a spectrum of clinical phenotypes.
checks.evidence_quote: This finding suggests that these disorders may not be distinct pathophysiologic entities, but rather represent a spectrum of related "myelinopathies" due to an underlying defect in myelination.
checks.explanation: The abstract presents CMT1B, DSS and CH as a spectrum of related disorders caused by MPZ mutations.

checks.claim: Warner et al. (1996) concluded that congenital hypomyelination is at the most severe end of the spectrum of MPZ-related phenotypes.
checks.explanation: The abstract links severity to mutation type but does not say congenital hypomyelination is the most severe phenotype.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Severely decreased motor nerve conduction velocities
Hypomyelination of peripheral nerves on nerve biopsy
